images.purpose: Implementation overview with corrected prototype boundaries
images.initial_prompt:
Use case: productivity-visual / scientific-educational.
Create ONE high-resolution 16:9 landscape implementation-overview hero image (target 2560 x 1440) for the same Management Agent condominium classifier project. This is the companion image a student can send to the lecturer to explain how the existing prototype was built. It must be visually elegant, technically accurate, and readable at presentation size.

Design: warm ivory background, deep midnight navy (#0B202B) typography and structural panels, pale mint (#76DDC0) accents, fine gridless connector lines, amber only for emergency bypass. Clean premium editorial systems diagram with large clear numbered stations, careful hierarchy, and generous margins. Use restrained depth rather than excessive rounded cards. No robots, no glowing brains, no imaginary servers, no decorative stock icons. Prioritize the real design and implementation over glamour.

Exact title and introductory copy:
Small brand: "MANAGEMENT AGENT"
Headline: "How the classifier works"
Subheading: "A focused implementation for condominium requests."

A prominent left-to-right six-stage flow, with clear arrow connections and compact readable labels:
"01" "Resident message"
"02" "Input validation"
"03" "Safety screen"
"04" "Classification"
"05" "Review policy"
"06" "Structured result"

Directly beneath Classification, a readable detail panel labelled "Choose a backend" with these two alternatives, separated cleanly:
"Offline: TF-IDF + logistic regression"
"Local LLM: Gemma 3 4B through Ollama"
Keep it visibly a choice, not two models in sequence.

Under Safety screen, a thin amber bypass connector must skip Classification and enter Review policy. Label that connector "Emergency match: bypass the model". Do not connect it to an autonomous dispatch action. Normal requests continue through Classification.

Under Structured result, show a compact, aligned example:
"Category: Maintenance"
"Priority: Normal"
"Suggested team: Maintenance team"
"Review flag and reasons"

Along the bottom, use a restrained implementation strip with exact copy:
"Streamlit interface"
"LangGraph workflow"
"Pydantic validation"
"LangChain + Ollama"
And a short separate review statement:
"Every LLM result requires staff confirmation."
Small footer:
"Classification only. No automatic tickets or approvals."

Ensure all text is spelled correctly, aligned and legible. Do not add invented metrics, calibration claims, accuracy percentages, deployment claims, UAT approval, multi-agent features, RAG, Chroma, or Jev equivalence. This illustration explains the existing classifier architecture. No personal names or private-message imagery. Output one finished, opaque-background image.
